WORKLOG — task 1 of vehicle_listing_desk (env_0015_car_sharing_marketplace). Written as each decision was taken and kept in step with every revision.

1. THE DRAW (Step 0). `.venv/bin/python skills/erl-task-instantiate/scripts/draw_counts.py env/env_0015_car_sharing_marketplace/tasks/vehicle_listing_desk --task 1` printed {"task": 1, "prerequisite_problems": 3, "problems": 4, "factor_counts": [4, 5, 4, 6]}. So three prerequisite problems and factor counts {4,4,5,6} as a multiset, assigned: listings_ext_document_verification 4, listings_ext_interval_grant 6, listings_ext_booked_consumption 5, listings_ext_reported_consumption 4. The tree was designed to the draw.

2. WHY THIS MAKES A GOOD TEST. A fleet host rings to give the monthly odometer reading the marketplace asks him for, and that is all he asks. The desk that simply books the reading against the last figure on file writes 770 miles less whatever allowances it finds, and is wrong. To reach 40 the agent must read out of the published policy that a host's reading is not counted before a reading dated today stands on the condition record; that a reading the marketplace books is not counted before a completed inspection dated within seven days stands; and that the interval such an inspection grants is not fixed before a registration verification dated within thirty days stands — at which point a document received six days ago and sitting unrecorded, and a workshop check carried out on Friday and recorded only in the care plan history, both become work that must be done first. None of that is in what the customer says; all of it is in the records and the rules. The four numbers then have to be got right from four different ladders apiece.

3. SCOPE (Principle C). Task 0 occupied the valuation-and-price axis: listings_evt_defect, listings_evt_valuation and listings_price, with the policies listings_ext_fault_intake, listings_ext_valuation_assessment, listings_ext_class_assignment and listings_ext_price_reset and their four tools. Task 1 claims what was reserved for it and nothing else: listings_evt_documents and listings_evt_inspection in both of its faces, with the policies listings_ext_document_verification, listings_ext_interval_grant, listings_ext_booked_consumption and listings_ext_reported_consumption and the tools verify_listing_document_28456ce9, record_vehicle_inspection_59fe0be1, record_booked_mileage_82af4bea and report_vehicle_mileage_90a8825c. The two scopes are disjoint in policies, in tools and in base lineage, and between them they cover every extended policy this difficulty declares. Nothing is reserved for a task that does not exist.

4. THE PROBLEM-TREE CARD (Principle H). A single chain of four, root last:
   listings_ext_document_verification -> listings_ext_interval_grant -> listings_ext_booked_consumption -> listings_ext_reported_consumption.
   Edge 1 (the interval waits on the registration check). kind value_input, gate paper_currency_addition, form state. Sentence, verbatim from listings_ext_interval_grant's own rule: "The interval a completed inspection grants is fixed only after a verification of the vehicle's registration dated within thirty calendar days of the handling date stands on its condition record." Four-point test: (1) the connective is "only after", joining this policy's own result (the interval it grants) to what it waits on; (2) the XX side is a record-visible state — a verification row of a registration and its date, in the words the condition-record finder uses — and names no action, performer or tool; (3) no tool name, policy id or snake_case token; (4) a hard "only after" over exactly one dated state, neither wider nor narrower than the edge's condition. Exactly one write of this difficulty brings that state about: verify_listing_document_28456ce9 is the only tool in the file that creates a listings_document_verified row. Derivation a reader performs: the sentence says the interval waits on a registration verification inside thirty days; the records show the most recent one dated 20 January 2025; the only policy whose result is a document recorded as verified is the document verification policy, so its write comes first. Why false at the opening: initial_state.listings_inspections.dc5c1db7-a797-4f0e-91d5-9ad2d2bd3c0c.record_date = 2025-01-20 with .document_kind = registration, and the other two verifications on file are a lender consent and an insurance certificate. Deletion sensitivity, actually run: 5,600 miles instead of 6,700.
   Edge 2 (the booked reading waits on the inspection). kind value_input, gate anchor_reading, form state. Sentence: "The miles a reading the marketplace books takes off the interval are not counted before a completed inspection dated within seven calendar days of the handling date stands on the vehicle's condition record." Four-point test: (1) the connective is "not before", the negated direction, and it rewrites exactly into "are counted only after a completed inspection dated within seven calendar days stands" with no condition added, dropped or split; (2) a record-visible state; (3) no code names; (4) hard, and scoped to exactly the state the condition names. Exactly one write brings it about: record_vehicle_inspection_59fe0be1 is the only tool that creates a listings_inspection_completed row. Why false: initial_state.listings_inspections.c6193910-2846-4c7a-aa9e-c9c6853d990d.record_date = 2025-03-04 is the most recent completed inspection, 385 days back. Deletion sensitivity, run: 0 miles instead of 90.
   Edge 3 (the host's report waits on the booked reading). kind value_input, gate reported_stretch, form state. Sentence: "The miles a reading the host reports take off the interval are not counted before an odometer record dated the handling date stands on the vehicle's condition record." Same four-point test, negated direction, a record-visible state. Exactly one write brings it about: record_booked_mileage_82af4bea is the only tool that creates an odometer record the marketplace itself books (report_vehicle_mileage_90a8825c is the host's own report, which is the very result this sentence governs, so it cannot be its own prerequisite). Why false: initial_state.listings_inspections.120bbfbb-d664-43fb-9482-5fbae64f7f61.record_date = 2026-01-15 is the latest odometer record, sixty-eight days back. Deletion sensitivity, run: 640 miles instead of 40.
   Direction was chosen result by result: an interval a marketplace grants "is fixed only after" the papers behind it are current, while miles counted against a customer's clock read naturally as "are not counted before". Across the difficulty's charter both directions are used and neither dominates.
   The customer's own write is the root: report_vehicle_mileage_90a8825c is owner=user, because the periodic odometer report is the host's own act on his own vehicle — the base rule names "the host's own periodic reading" as one of the three sources of a reading — and the desk unlocks it and hands it over at the root's place in the order. It completes on the spot.
   Tools validate nothing: see prerequisite_closure.tools_do_not_block.

5. BASE-INVARIANT CARD. Write 1, subject listings_document_verified, governed by listings_evt_documents alone; its one gate scoped to that subject, document_verified_by_marketplace, requires the check to be the marketplace's rather than the host's word, evidenced by system record and correlated by listings_inspections.vehicle_id, which is the tool's vehicle_id argument; the verification of 20 January 2025 on the same vehicle is the pre-action evidence that this vehicle's documents are checked this way. Writes 2, 3 and 4 all have subjects governed by listings_evt_inspection, whose one applicable gate, inspection_clock_only_while_listed, requires the listing to stand in listed, snoozed or suspended; it stands at suspended, which the gate's own state_contract allows, so records may be written. No time-kind eligibility applies to any of the four subjects, so temporal_feasibility is empty; the one interval in play, the class's three business day document verification period, is not a structured gate but is respected in the world: the certificate was received on 18 March 2026 and the handling date is 24 March 2026, four business days later, so the check has run. The base clause "A completed inspection grants the class's mileage interval afresh and sets the next due date the class's day interval ahead" is superseded clause by clause in listings_ext_interval_grant.overwrite; every other clause of listings_evt_inspection, and the whole of listings_evt_documents, stays in force and is inherited.

6. BUSINESS-OBJECT CARD. One listing, vehicle acafe194-2c45-400b-99f6-fe1558f6a2ac, the host's only one. Every listings aggregate is scoped to it by vehicle_id. The booked odometer record written at action 18 carries source_inspection_id pointing at the inspection written at action 16, so the reading is correlated to the exact record it is taken from rather than to the vehicle at large. Cross-category objects are correlated by vehicle_id: care plan 1b2ae902-600e-4bf5-84e3-393104bc65a0, roadside subscription 3130143d-538b-4692-92a7-075d4a6734ab and protection enrolment 9c13aa9b-4392-4a84-81f9-b77e0eb4925e are all held on this vehicle; payout account 74280285-2f6e-42b2-bfc9-6e81b4ae0181 is the host's single account. Rows deliberately excluded by the windows: the care plan visit of 22 August 2024 falls inside the twenty-four month window but outside the three month one, so a reader who uses one window for both service ladders gets the workshop allowance wrong; the insurance certificate that failed on 14 June 2025 is inside the twenty-four month document window and is the near-miss that separates the three-image tier from the one-image tier; the completed inspection of 6 September 2024 is the older of two and must not be read as the most recent.

7. FACTOR CARD. Nineteen declared factors over four computations, each proved load-bearing by the Step 5 sensitivity run:
   listings_ext_document_verification (4): registration_image_standard, method, tier "a registration verified within the rolling twenty-four months", standard five, baseline 12 against 14; check_pattern_addition, parameter, multi-source, tier "two or more verified documents with at least one failing", plus three, baseline 11; lender_consent_addition, parameter, tier "exactly one verified lender consent", plus two, baseline 12; registration_lapse_addition, parameter, multi-source, tier "more than seven days past expiry and the listing suspended", plus four, baseline 10. Whole-baseline fall-back 3.
   listings_ext_interval_grant (6): paper_currency_addition, parameter, multi-source, the binding the first edge carries; overrun_reduction_step, parameter, multi-source; serviced_vehicle_addition, parameter, cross-difficulty on service (visits dde4ebbf-d148-4032-8079-a65ba7a6f4f2, fb98f58e-5c76-4390-a272-4305576e9459, f5bc2180-27e9-4d8b-b5de-272a743720b3 and 5fd0b5c0-9c4b-4c74-8d9f-2b39ae0be0d1 under plan 1b2ae902-600e-4bf5-84e3-393104bc65a0); odometer_band_reduction, parameter; recovery_history_reduction, parameter, cross-difficulty on roadside (callouts 73f04ae8-7c23-4ff8-9474-14ac30b77fd6 and b274b691-4351-43ff-a459-50ef7ab2f25b); fault_standing_basis, method, multi-source. Whole-baseline fall-back 10,000, the very figure baseline.rule gives on its own, against gold 6,700.
   listings_ext_booked_consumption (5): anchor_reading_basis, method, the binding the second edge carries; workshop_transit_allowance, parameter, cross-difficulty on service; recovery_transit_allowance, parameter, cross-difficulty on roadside; idle_listing_allowance, parameter, multi-source; repair_transit_allowance, parameter, cross-difficulty on hostplan (claim 41b711b2-4f17-4361-938e-3d63f75d3f01 under enrolment 9c13aa9b-4392-4a84-81f9-b77e0eb4925e). Whole-baseline fall-back 0 against gold 90.
   listings_ext_reported_consumption (4): reported_stretch_basis, method, multi-source, the binding the third edge carries; registration_lapse_private_allowance, parameter, multi-source; inspection_transit_allowance_step, parameter, multi-source; idle_period_allowance_step, parameter, multi-source, cross-difficulty on payouts (ledger rows d488d6dd-3e07-40c9-9cb9-995c5e22108a, 50b2f1cf-c2c1-4313-a286-9a6f03fa6091 and 8d0f3eea-8d4c-49cd-8d7b-1aee8a70e706 on account 74280285-2f6e-42b2-bfc9-6e81b4ae0181). Whole-baseline fall-back 770 against gold 40.
   Multi-source floor and cross-difficulty floor are both met several times over, and four different other products are read — service, roadside, hostplan and payouts — every one of them by value (XCOUNT and XSUM) rather than by bare existence, with the rows seeded for this customer. No stamp names any tier outcome.

8. THE WORLD (Step 3). One customer, one listing, eleven condition records over eighteen months, a review case, and four cross-category holdings with their ledgers. Why each class of row exists and what its removal changes: the two completed inspections set the last inspection date and the interval history — remove the one of 4 March 2025 and the overrun, the fault-standing comparison and the due date all move; the five telematics odometer readings carry the credit to exactly minus 340 (the sum of all eleven miles_delta values, matching the listing field) and set the highest standing reading of 88,540 — remove the last and the anchor, the odometer band and the reported stretch all move; the three document verifications set the registration currency, the failed-check pattern and the lender consent count, each read by a different ladder; the warning light of 19 December 2025 is the single fault the interval's method factor reads. The review case of 18 March 2026 is the system record that the renewed certificate was received and that its verification period has run. Cross-category: the care plan and its four visits feed three ladders across two policies on different windows; the roadside subscription and its two callouts feed two; the protection enrolment and its single claim feed one; the payout account and its three trip earnings feed one, with the most recent earning dated 8 December 2025 so that the rolling three month window is genuinely empty while the twelve month window is not. A DELIBERATE CACHE DIVERGENCE is seeded and is the trap of this task: listings_vehicles.odometer_miles stands at 89,310, the live figure the fitted telematics unit keeps on the listing (the class requires telematics), while the highest reading booked on the condition record is 88,540. An agent who takes the listing field as the last booked reading computes the booked consumption as nothing and the host's report as nothing; the ledger is what the policy reads. Automatic clauses checked row by row: the inspection clock (overrun, and the listing is already suspended, so no further suspension is owed); the registration grace (expired 28 February 2026 plus the class's seven days, which is exactly why the listing stands suspended on that ground); the safety defect grace (the only fault is a warning light of 19 December 2025, not a safety defect in the recall sense, and the listing's suspension ground is unrelated); the defect-count compliance review (one report in the rolling twelve months against a threshold of four).

9. PERSONA (Step 4). Anton Kaminski is written as a working owner in a hurry with one errand. Volunteered at the opening: the reading on the dash, that he is at the van, and the request itself — all entailed by initial_state (odometer_miles 89310, one listings_vehicles row, model_year 2021). Given only when asked: his name, his mobile, his licence number, his zip, his email, that he does not know his member reference, that the van has been off the marketplace for weeks, that Pima Fleet had it in on Friday, and that he renewed the registration and sent the certificate in. Reacted to only after the agent speaks: taking the figure as given, keying the reading in himself once it is handed over, and closing. He is not an oracle: he never names the marketplace's inspection record, never says a document needs checking, never says a reading needs booking, and reacts identically whether the agent's figures are right or wrong. His arc closes exactly where evaluation_criteria closes — he confirms his own reading and rings off, and he explicitly asks nothing about getting the van relisted, so nothing he says is work gold does not contain.

10. VERIFICATION ACTUALLY RUN (Step 5). The four computations were evaluated in topological order over initial_state plus the preceding gold writes, with the real tools replayed between steps. Output:
    listings_ext_document_verification -> 14   whole-baseline 3    factor baselines 12 / 11 / 12 / 10
    listings_ext_interval_grant -> 6700   whole-baseline 10000   factor baselines 5600 / 8200 / 5200 / 7500 / 7800 / 9000
    listings_ext_booked_consumption -> 90   whole-baseline 0   factor baselines 0 / 210 / 170 / 340 / 150
    listings_ext_reported_consumption -> 40   whole-baseline 770   factor baselines 640 / 100 / 80 / 70
    Prerequisite sensitivity, each depended-on write skipped and everything else replayed unchanged: skip the verification -> interval 5600; skip the inspection -> booked miles 0; skip the booked reading -> reported miles 640. Every edge moves a scored figure, and check_compute recomputes each of these at handling time.

11. TWO-WAY EQUIVALENCE OF RULE AND COMPUTE. Forward, every binding that reads the world or makes a choice quotes its rule sentence verbatim in compute_basis. Reverse sweep: in listings_ext_document_verification, d1/d2/d3 are claimed by the standard figure and result, d4 by image_subtotal, d5 to d8 by the four factor bindings. In listings_ext_interval_grant, g1/g2/g3 by base_interval and result, g4 is the sentence the interval overwrite declares, g5 by adjusted_interval, g6 is the prerequisite sentence, g7 to g12 by the six factor bindings. In listings_ext_booked_consumption, m1 to m4 by the baseline chain, m5 is the prerequisite sentence, m6 to m10 by the five factor bindings. In listings_ext_reported_consumption, h1 to h3 by the baseline chain, h4 is the prerequisite sentence, h5 to h8 by the four factor bindings. Sensitive words cross-checked: every "rolling twelve months", "rolling twenty-four months" and "rolling three months" has within_months= on its aggregate; every "highest standing" has MAX and every "most recent" has LATEST with its date field; "rounded down to the nearer hundred miles" has the explicit integer division; "rounded half away from zero to a whole mile" has RND(...,0); "a stretch of less than nothing being counted as nothing" has MX(...,0); and no filter appears in an expression that the quoted sentence does not state.

12. THE ORDER OF OPERATIONS PINNED IN PROSE. The document rule says the additions are "summed and the total is added once to that figure, rather than each addition being applied to the figure the one before it produced". The interval rule says "the share is applied once to the standard interval and the product rounded half away from zero to a whole mile, and the additions and reductions ... are then summed and applied once to that product", which fixes both the order and the single rounding. Both consumption rules say the allowances "are summed and taken off the stretch once" and that a result "of less than nothing" is nothing, which fixes the floor and its moment. Each rounding names its mode, its precision and where it happens.

13. DRAFT RECOMPUTATION FROM THE VISIBLE CONTEXT ALONE. Masking the extended yaml, compute, expected, gold and this dossier, and working only from the prose that will be published, the tool schemas, what the finders return and what the caller says: the caller wants his reading taken; the reported-reading rule says the miles are not counted before an odometer record dated today stands, and the record shows the latest is 15 January; the booked-reading rule says its miles are not counted before a completed inspection inside seven days stands, and the record shows 4 March 2025; the interval rule says the interval is fixed only after a registration verification inside thirty days stands, and the record shows 20 January 2025 while the review queue shows a certificate received on 18 March. That chain is forced in one direction and gives the same four writes in the same order, and working the published ladders gives 14, 6,700, 90 and 40 — equal to gold. No second reading was found: the anchors are named record by record, the windows carry their endpoints, and each ladder's tiers are pairwise disjoint as written.

14. WHAT A CARELESS AGENT GETS WRONG, AND HOW THE POLICY EXCLUDES IT. Reading the odometer standing on the listing as the last booked reading gives a stretch of nothing at both consumption steps. Using the three month care-visit count for the twenty-four month service addition, or the reverse, moves both the interval and the booked miles. Taking the interval as the class's ten thousand miles, as the base charter alone would suggest, ignores the declared override and every adjustment. Forgetting that the fault-standing method rounds down to the nearer hundred gives 6,750. Measuring the host's stretch from the telematics reading rather than from the reading just booked gives 770 before allowances. Each is excluded by a sentence of the published rule — the anchor ladders, the window endpoints, the stated rounding and the declared override — rather than by anything the customer says.

15. CLOSURE. policy -> target_tool -> computation.step/arg -> gold call -> terminal state: listings_ext_document_verification -> verify_listing_document_28456ce9 -> step 14 verification_image_count -> a listings_document_verified row dated 2026-03-24 holding fourteen images of the registration; listings_ext_interval_grant -> record_vehicle_inspection_59fe0be1 -> step 16 interval_miles_granted -> a listings_inspection_completed row granting 6,700 miles; listings_ext_booked_consumption -> record_booked_mileage_82af4bea -> step 18 booked_miles_consumed -> a listings_odometer_reported row at 89,140 taking 90 miles off the interval; listings_ext_reported_consumption -> report_vehicle_mileage_90a8825c -> step 20 reported_miles_consumed -> the host's own listings_odometer_reported row at 89,310 taking 40 miles off. charter_scope.extended_policies equals the set of computations.policy_id equals the four problems of the tree, required_documents repeats it verbatim in order, and charter_scope.task_tools is the four tools in first-call order. The whole consultation runs at one frozen_time: the document check had already run before the call, the workshop inspection had already been carried out, and everything the desk does is a record raised on the spot — nothing waits on clearing, approval, delivery or a future date.

REVISION ROUND 2 (source-layer policy audit, report ids T1-F1, T1-F2, T1-F3, CG-1b, CG-5, CG-6, CG-OBS-4, CG-OBS-6, T1-OBS-1 to T1-OBS-4). Base is frozen; every change is inside this difficulty's write domain. The tree, the seed, the persona, the read set and three of the four scored values are untouched; only the interval computation moves, and it moves because the factor that carries the first edge was rebuilt.

T1-F1 and CG-1b (base `listings_evt_inspection` sentence 4 directs this reading to be queried rather than recorded). Symptom: the whole errand had two terminal states — a query with no row in the host's name, or a filed reading consuming miles. Root cause: `listings_ext_reported_consumption` inherited that sentence with `overwrite: []`, so the deviation was never declared. Change: an `overwrite` entry now quotes the base sentence verbatim — "A telematics reading is authoritative where one exists; a host reading standing more than the class's variance tolerance away from the telematics figure is queried rather than recorded, and the listing is not suspended while the query is open." — and names the sentence of this policy's own rule that replaces it: "A reading the host reports is recorded on the vehicle's condition record whatever distance stands between it and the reading the most recent telematics odometer record carries, and that distance is settled by the way the stretch is measured rather than by holding the reading back." The errand is unchanged and so is the scored figure of 40; what changes is that the charter now says outright which of the two readings governs, so the base clause no longer entails a second terminal state. The extended policy's own treatment of a divergence is not silence: the fall-through of `reported_stretch_basis` measures from the telematics reading and its second tier reduces the stretch by the class tolerance, "the difference being queried rather than charged", so the tolerance still does work — it decides how much of the distance is charged rather than whether the reading is filed.

T1-F2 and CG-5 (`paper_currency_share` sat on a baseline its own `baseline.rule` contradicted, and bore no weight against the honest one). Symptom: `baseline.rule` said "the whole of it is open" (share 1.0) while the factor declared its baseline as three quarters and its fall-through was three quarters too, so the computation document admitted two fall-back numbers (10,000 and 7,500) and, against the honest baseline, substituting the factor left the scored value untouched. Root cause: the ladder was built so that resolving the prerequisite moved the world onto the ladder's *fall-through*, which is exactly the tier a baseline must be; a share whose default is the whole interval can only ever be reduced, and the prerequisite's write is what makes the papers current. Change: the share is gone. `current_papers_share` / `ageing_papers_share` / `stale_papers_share` are replaced by `documented_papers_addition` (1,500), `current_papers_addition` (750) and `no_papers_addition` (0); `base_interval` is now the standard interval itself, `K('standard_interval_miles')`, and the new binding `paper_currency_addition` joins the summed adjustments. The ladder now reads: a registration verified within thirty calendar days on a record carrying twelve or more images of it adds one thousand five hundred miles; one verified within thirty days on a record carrying fewer than twelve images adds seven hundred and fifty; any other vehicle adds nothing. Its `baseline` is `K('no_papers_addition')`, which is its own fall-through **and** exactly what `baseline.rule` states ("the whole of it is open to a vehicle whose own record calls for nothing further" — the standard ten thousand miles, with nothing added). Consequences, all re-run: the factor now sits on tier 1 (the verification written at action 14 is dated today and carries fourteen images), so it bears weight — substituting its honest baseline gives 5,600 against gold 6,700; the whole-baseline fall-back is 10,000, which is precisely the number a reader of `baseline.rule` and `baseline.params` computes, so the computation document has one definite answer again; and the first edge still bears weight, skipping the verification giving 5,600. The factor is also multi-source now (the verification's date and the image count that record carries are distinct evidence), which it was not before. Downstream: the interval granted rises from 5,600 to 6,700, so the gold argument at action 16 and the inspection row's minted id change; `record_booked_mileage_82af4bea`'s `source_inspection_id` follows it to insp_2f777902fded. The booked consumption (90) and the reported consumption (40) are unchanged, because the one binding that reads the granted interval, `granted_interval_standing`, tests it against five thousand miles and 6,700 clears that line as 5,600 did.

T1-F3 and CG-6 (`baseline.params` named a default no baseline sentence uses). Change: `listings_ext_reported_consumption.baseline.params` is now `[]`. `reading_variance_tolerance_miles` stays in the policy's `params`, where the ladder tier that consumes it lives, and is no longer published as one of the computation document's defaults — so the document cannot hand a reader a 75 it has no sentence for, and cannot leak the constant that separates the ladder's tiers from its fall-through.

CG-OBS-4 (the state the root edge waits on was brought about by two writes of this difficulty). Change: the prerequisite sentence now waits on "an odometer record dated the handling date **and naming the condition record its reading was taken from**", which only `record_booked_mileage_82af4bea` produces — the host's own report carries no source record. The edge's `condition`, `why_false` and `flips_to_true_by` are restated to match, and the seed evidence is unchanged (the five telematics readings on file name no source record and none is dated the handling date). The state form is preserved: the sentence names a record and a field, no action, no performer and no tool.

CG-OBS-6 (the lapse ladder was non-monotone). Change: `registration_lapse_addition`'s second tier is now "the registration on file more than seven calendar days past its expiry and the listing not suspended" (two images) and the fall-through is "a vehicle whose registration on file is not past its expiry" (none), so a longer lapse can no longer add less than a shorter one. The compute branch is rewritten to match, the tier this world takes is unchanged (24 days past expiry, listing suspended, four images) and the figure stays 14.

CG-4 (the first edge's `effect` asserted a particular tier transition): restated as general product law — the paper currency addition binding "is read on that verification rather than on an older one, and the standard interval is adjusted by what that verification's own record carries".

T1-OBS-1 (write 1's `inspection_channel` settled by exclusion) and T1-OBS-4 (CG-OBS-7, the larger private-use allowance going to the re-verified vehicle): no change warranted; the audit demonstrates a unique residual in the first and a defensible business reading in the second.

T1-OBS-2 (the whole-baseline fall-back for `booked_consumption` is zero): no change warranted, and the reason is structural. The three anchors the ladder can choose between are the highest reading standing on the odometer records, the reading the most recent odometer record carries and the odometer standing on the listing; before the booked write the first two are the same figure (88,540), so making either of them the fall-through would make the factor decorative on this world, which is the defect the audit is most concerned to prevent. The listing odometer (89,310) is the only fall-through that keeps the factor load-bearing, and it yields nothing chargeable because the listing's live telematics figure already stands above the reading being booked — a definite figure, and the one the charter's own words give.

REVISION ROUND 3 (render-layer audit; `audits/policy_kb/vehicle_listing_desk/1.md` policy-side notes 1–4 and `audits/runtime_context/vehicle_listing_desk/1.md` RED 2, plus the charter-wide sweep the brief asked for). No scored value, no baseline, no factor sensitivity, no seed row and no computed gold argument moved in this round: the recomputation still gives 14, 6,700, 90 and 40, and the inspection row id is unchanged. The changes are rule prose, one persona clause and the tracing that cites them.

MINE — RED 2, THE SCORED ARGUMENT NO RULE DECIDED. `inspection_channel` on `verify_listing_document_28456ce9` is scored, and neither the source nor the corpus decided it: the gold `mobile_inspector` was recoverable only by copying the channel of the registration verification of 20 January 2025, while the persona's own words ("sent the certificate through the app") pointed the blind auditor at `self_photo`, which is exactly what the enum's gloss describes. Of the three routes open — state the deciding rule, change the persona to state the value it means, or stop scoring the argument — I took the first, and repaired the persona so the two no longer point in different directions. user_scenario:
Anton Kaminski runs a two-man hauling outfit out of Scottsdale and keeps a Ford Transit on Keyturn to earn its keep in the weeks his own work is thin. He is standing in the yard with the van's driver door open when he rings, one boot on the sill, and he comes to it before the greeting is finished: "It's the monthly mileage you people ask for. I'm at the van right now and the dash says 89,310 — can you take it while I've got you?" That is the whole of what he wants today, and he says he has a load to pick up in twenty minutes, so he would rather not be on the phone long.

He is brisk rather than rude, and he answers what he is asked without embroidering it. He is content for the desk to look at whatever it needs on his account while he waits, and says as much if the agent asks; but the reading is his to give, and when the agent sets the reporting up and hands it over he keys it in himself and reads back what comes up on his screen.

Asked who he is, he gives his name as Anton Kaminski and the mobile on the account, 4805532971; when the desk wants a second thing he reads the Arizona licence number, 55731640, straight off the card. If more is wanted he can give the zip on the billing address, 85251, or the email the account was opened under, anton.kaminski@northscottsdale-hauling.com. He does not know the Keyturn reference for himself or for the van and says so without apology; he has never had to quote one.

He knows the van the way a working owner knows a van and nothing whatever about how the marketplace keeps its books. He can say it is the only vehicle he lists, a 2021 Transit he bought new for the business, and that it has been off the marketplace for a few weeks, which he mentions flatly if the agent asks about it because the same thing is showing on his own screen. He has no idea what the marketplace's inspection clock says about the van, and if he is asked he says that is what he pays Keyturn to keep track of. If the agent asks whether the van has been anywhere lately, he says Pima Fleet had it in on Friday for its usual once-over under the care plan and that as far as he heard they were happy with it; if the agent asks about the paperwork on it, he says he renewed the state registration at the beginning of the month and sent the certificate in through the app the same week for Keyturn to check, which he assumes it has. He offers neither of those unless he is asked, and he does not suggest that anything needs doing about either.

He does not chase the agent while the desk works, and he asks nothing about getting the van back in front of guests; the load is what is on his mind and the reading is the errand. When the agent comes back with what the reading takes off the van's interval, he takes the figure as given — "if you say so" — and does not argue it or ask for it again. Once he has keyed the reading in himself and seen it come back confirmed, he says that is that, thanks them for being quick about it, and rings off.
